t: The Neo-Babylonian Empire rose on Assyria's ruins and, under Nebuchadnezzar II, dominated the Near East.
Its destruction of Jerusalem and the Babylonian captivity reshaped Judaism into a portable, text-centred faith.
Weak successors and a king who neglected Marduk let Cyrus the Great take Babylon almost unopposed in 539 BCE.
dyk: Babylonian sky-watching was so well known that 'Chaldean' became a byword for astronomer and astrologer in the Greek and Roman worlds.
ev: Nabopolassar seizes Babylon and restores native Babylonian kingship
Babylonians and Medes sack Nineveh, the Assyrian capital
Crown prince Nebuchadnezzar II defeats Necho II's Egyptians at Carchemish
Nebuchadnezzar captures Jerusalem and deports King Jehoiachin
Babylonians destroy Jerusalem and its Temple after a second siege
Babylonians begin a thirteen-year siege of the island city of Tyre
Nebuchadnezzar II dies; four kings follow in six years
Cyrus the Great wins at Opis and Babylon falls without real resistance
